title: Shared cell resistance adds no error-bound failures in 129 selected Allen mouse electrical components
abstract: We tested whether electrical pairs that share a cell need a larger bounded correction when they must use one input resistance per cell. In Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1, 135 selected mouse pairs formed 129 components. Only four components had shared cells. Each joint minimum error factor equaled the largest separate-pair minimum in its component. The same result held for steady resistance and three selection checks. At factor 1.10, both tests failed in 68 primary components. We give an exact path and cycle certificate based on standard difference constraints and check it against linear programming. A synthetic chain proves that shared cells can strengthen this test in other graphs. This is a necessary algebraic transfer screen, not a full passive circuit fit or evidence about rectification. Sparse graphs, missing summaries and unmatched measurement states limit biological use. Code, proof, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and separate-data retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Separate pair and joint shared-cell screens agree in 129 selected Allen mouse components. Only four components contain shared cells. Counts refer to connected components, not independent animals. Source: Allen Institute for Brain Science, Synaptic Physiology r2.1; Campagnola, Seeman and colleagues, doi:10.1126/science.abj5861.
